issues.title: [dynamo] TVM backend fails to import with all pip-installable TVM versions (relay removed in TVM 0.20)
issues.author: guan404ming
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `tvm` dynamo backend depends on `tvm.relay` and `tvm.contrib.graph_executor`, removed upstream in TVM v0.20. PyPI only offers `apache-tvm==0.25.*` now, so every install fails at import, and the error message suggests installing apache-tvm, which cannot fix it. `tvm.meta_schedule` is also gone, so the tuning paths have no equivalent.

```python
import torch

torch.compile(lambda x: x + 1, backend="tvm")(torch.randn(2))
```

TVM 0.25 ships its own working dynamo backend (`tvm.relax.frontend.torch.relax_dynamo`, verified locally with `torch.compile`). Should this backend delegate to it, or be deprecated?

### Error logs

```
BackendCompilerFailed: backend='tvm' raised:
ImportError: cannot import name 'relay' from 'tvm'
```

(re-raised as "Please install apache-tvm to use the tvm backend.")

### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.14.0a0+gitc5bf344
OS: macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)
Clang version: 17.0.0 (clang-1700.0.13.5)
Python version: 3.11.13 (64-bit runtime)
Is CUDA available: False
CPU: Apple M1 Max

[pip3] numpy==2.4.6
[pip3] torch==2.14.0a0+gitc5bf344
[pip3] apache-tvm==0.25.0.post1
```

issues.title: [dynamo] ts and aot_ts backends broken by LazyGraphModule
issues.author: guan404ming
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `ts` and `aot_ts` backends fail on any function: `torch.jit.script` cannot script the `_LazyGraphModule` dynamo passes to backends since `use_lazy_graph_module` became the default (#117911). That PR wrapped the tests in `_force_skip_lazy_graph_module()`, so CI stays green while every user call fails.

```python
import torch

torch.compile(lambda x: torch.relu(x) + 1, backend="ts")(torch.randn(4))
```

Rebuilding a plain `GraphModule` before scripting fixes both backends, verified locally.

### Error logs

```
BackendCompilerFailed: backend='ts' raised:
RuntimeError:
method cannot be used as a value:
  File ".../torch/fx/_lazy_graph_module.py", line 120
        return cls.forward is cls._lazy_forward
               ~~~~~~~~~~~ <--- HERE
```

### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.14.0a0+gitc5bf344
OS: macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)
```

issues.title: Inductor mm template uses CUDA TF32 flag on XPU, diverging from eager
issues.author: wdziurdz
issues.body:
Inductor decides ALLOW_TF32 for the GEMM Triton template from torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision, regardless of device. The XPU heuristic inherits this unchanged, so a compiled fp32 matmul on XPU uses TF32 while eager XPU matmul does not. Eager XPU reads a different flag (allowTF32OneDNN, i.e. torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32), so the two paths disagree.

Location: torch/_inductor/template_heuristics/triton.py, MMTemplateConfigMixin.get_extra_kwargs:

    allow_tf32 = torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision == "tf32" and (size_threshold)

XPUMMTemplateConfigHeuristic inherits this; there is no device branch.

Repro (XPU):

    import torch
    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("high")  # sets cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32"
    a = torch.randn(1024, 1024, device="xpu")
    b = torch.randn(1024, 1024, device="xpu")
    ref = a @ b
    act = torch.compile(lambda x, y: x @ y)(a, b)
    torch.testing.assert_close(act, ref, atol=4e-3, rtol=4e-3)  # fails

Eager stays fp32 (allow_tf32_onednn defaults to False); compiled uses TF32. This surfaces as inductor/test_max_autotune.py::test_autotune_device_guard failing on XPU.

Expected: the TF32 decision should follow the precision flag the device eager path uses. On XPU that is torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32, read by the XPU matmul kernel via at::Context::allowTF32OneDNN().

issues.title: [CI][ROCm] DebertaV2ForMaskedLM fails to import from transformers on gfx950 (dynamic_inductor_huggingface eager_fail_to_run)
issues.author: frgossen
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`DebertaV2ForMaskedLM` can no longer be imported from `transformers` in the ROCm (gfx950) benchmark image, so it fails to run in **eager** on the periodic `dynamic_inductor_huggingface` job:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: Could not import module 'DebertaV2ForMaskedLM'. Are this object's requirements defined correctly?
  File ".../transformers/utils/import_utils.py", line 2342, in __getattr__
  File ".../benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py", line 146, in get_module_cls_by_model_name
    return getattr(module, model_cls_name)
...
DebertaV2ForMaskedLM  EAGER_FAILED
DebertaV2ForMaskedLM  FAIL:  accuracy=eager_fail_to_run, expected=pass_due_to_skip
```

**Job:** `inductor-periodic / rocm-periodic-dynamo-benchmarks-test / test (dynamic_inductor_huggingface, 1, 1, linux.rocm.gpu.gfx950.1)`

The model's expected status was `pass_due_to_skip`, but it now reports `eager_fail_to_run`, which reds the whole job.

### Root cause

This is a **`transformers` import failure**, not a PyTorch/inductor regression — `getattr(transformers, "DebertaV2ForMaskedLM")` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` (the DebertaV2 modeling module's requirements aren't satisfied in the pinned transformers used by the ROCm image). Since eager can't even load the model, it never gets to compile.

It appears ROCm-image-specific: the CUDA HF jobs still record `DebertaV2ForMaskedLM,pass_due_to_skip,0` and pass.

### Fix / mitigation

Short term, re-baseline the ROCm inference CSV so the job stops being blocked: PR #188850 sets `DebertaV2ForMaskedLM` to `eager_fail_to_run` in `benchmarks/dynamo/ci_expected_accuracy/rocm/dynamic_inductor_huggingface_inference.csv` (matching the other unimportable models, e.g. `BlenderbotForCausalLM`).

Real fix: investigate why `DebertaV2ForMaskedLM` fails to import in the ROCm image's transformers (version skew / missing dep) and restore it.

### Versions

ROCm gfx950 periodic dynamo-benchmarks image, PyTorch trunk `main`, observed 2026-07-02.

comments.body:
p.s. additional context from the claude investigation: https://gist.github.com/vkuzo/c39600335b86f42eb8e4adb63d720b51

this line seems fishy to me:

```
  Failure signature                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  For the grad_weight = x.t() @ grad_output GEMM (shapes M,K,N = 16,16,32 → grad_weight is 32×16):                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  - Triton 3.8: 224/512 elements are exactly 0; the zeros form a regular stride-4 column lattice (every 4th column of grad_weight is dead). max_abs_diff vs eager ≈ 13.75.                                                       
  - Triton 3.7.1: bit-identical to eager (0 zeros).                                                                                                                                                                              

  The zeroing is purely positional (depends on column index mod 4, not on data values) — columns of similar magnitude are alternately correct/zeroed. This is the fingerprint of a wrong store mask/predicate on a strided
  (transposed) store in the fused fp8-quantize + transpose + _scaled_mm kernel, not an fp8 scaling/underflow issue. The forward output and grad_input are correct; only grad_weight is affected.
```

issues.title: Inductor pointwise operations slower with TMA than without
issues.author: riccardofelluga
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Enabling Inductor's generic pointwise TMA path with
`torch._inductor.config.triton.use_tensor_descriptor=True` makes this simple
SiLU kernel slower than the default `torch.compile` path on both B200 and H100.

This is due to descriptor setup overhead: the generic codegen path builds
TMA tensor descriptors inside the generated Triton kernel, so each CTA pays
descriptor construction cost. For a simple memory-bound pointwise op, that
overhead can outweigh any benefit from TMA loads.

## Repro


```python
"""
Run:
  python repro_inductor_tma_slowdown.py
"""

import statistics

import torch
import torch._inductor.config as inductor_config


SHAPES = [
    (4096, 4096),
    (8192, 8192),
    (16384, 16384),
]


def compile_silu():
    return torch.compile(
        lambda x: torch.nn.functional.silu(x),
        mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs",
        fullgraph=True,
    )


def bench(fn, x, warmup=10, iters=100):
    for _ in range(warmup):
        fn(x)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    times_us = []
    for _ in range(iters):
        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        start.record()
        fn(x)
        end.record()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        times_us.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000)
    return statistics.median(times_us)


if not torch.cuda.is_available():
    raise SystemExit("CUDA is required")

print(f"PyTorch: {torch.__version__}")
print(f"CUDA: {torch.version.cuda}")
print()
print("| Shape | default compile us | compile + TMA us | slowdown |")
print("|---|---:|---:|---:|")

for shape in SHAPES:
    x = torch.randn(shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)

    torch._dynamo.reset()
    inductor_config.triton.use_tensor_descriptor = False
    inductor_config.assume_aligned_inputs = False
    default = compile_silu()
    default(x)
    default_us = bench(default, x)

    torch._dynamo.reset()
    inductor_config.triton.use_tensor_descriptor = True
    inductor_config.assume_aligned_inputs = True
    tma = compile_silu()
    tma(x)
    tma_us = bench(tma, x)
    slowdown = tma_us / default_us

    m, n = shape
    print(f"| {m}x{n} | {default_us:.1f} | {tma_us:.1f} | {slowdown:.2f}x |")

```

The script compares the same bf16 SiLU workload in two modes:

1. Default `torch.compile`
2. `torch.compile` with `triton.use_tensor_descriptor=True`

It resets Dynamo before compiling each mode so the two paths do not share a
cached compiled graph.

## Results

### B200

| Shape | default compile us | compile + TMA us | slowdown |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096x4096 | 56.1 | 78.8 | 1.41x |
| 8192x8192 | 87.5 | 141.4 | 1.62x |
| 16384x16384 | 220.0 | 358.4 | 1.63x |

### H100

| Shape | default compile us | compile + TMA us | slowdown |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096x4096 | 52.4 | 72.3 | 1.38x |
| 8192x8192 | 117.8 | 140.2 | 1.19x |
| 16384x16384 | 380.9 | 433.9 | 1.14x |

## Proposed Direction

The TMA descriptor should be created once on the host and passed into the
kernel, instead of being rebuilt inside every CTA. Inductor already has
host-side TMA descriptor infrastructure for template paths; the gap is wiring
that approach into the generic pointwise codegen path.


### Error logs

_No response_

comments.author: jananisriram
comments.body: @riccardofelluga I've opened a PR for host-side TMA for pointwise kernels (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/186904), which takes inspiration from https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/185825 but adds more robust edge case checks and some performance improvements. I'll rebase https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/186752 (host-side TMA for GEMM templates) and https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/186756 (host-side TMA epilogue store) onto this new implementation.
